- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially if recent price is falling.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next 5–10 days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the following 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-estimate mid-period with a smoother transition.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day forecasts when sentiment is neutral or mixed; model tends to hold bias; apply a 1–2% downward adjustment if recent 7-day average is above 30-day average.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 0.33 → 1.00 → 0.33), model overreacts; dampen forecast volatility by 10–20% in the next 7 days.
